title: Position picker (position-ref widget) lists the `everyone` audience anchor, which the server refuses as a grant target; filter the audience anchors out of the grant picker
body:
Filed by the epic PM of objectstack-ai/objectstack#15194 (`session_01Rerax7QTjKMPCUZxQUtPFR`, `marchtian`) at the maintainer's request on 2026-10-12: route this finding to the `domain:ui` lane. Priority: p1.

## What was seen
- Context: the B2 grant pickers. objectstack-ai/objectstack#22939 declares `widget: 'position-ref'` on `sys_user_position.position`, and this repo's #12175 (PR-5, merged as `088e0f705`) supplies the widget.
- In the browser, against PR-5's head, the position picker listed 16 positions **including `everyone`**. That is the audience anchor that ADR-0131 declares as `position` metadata beside `guest`.
- The server refuses an audience anchor as a grant target. This is recorded in the seat's ACCEPT on #22939 (objectstack-ai/objectstack comment 6118326033, "Recorded finding").
- So a user can pick a value that the save then refuses.

## Ask
- Measure first, against the current console. The objectstack pin moves to `088e0f705` in objectstack-ai/objectstack#22967. That PR's browser check also records whether `everyone` is listed.
- Then filter the audience anchors (`everyone`, `guest`, and whatever the registry marks as an audience anchor) out of the grant picker's options.
- Read how the registry marks an anchor. Do not hard-code the names unless no marker exists, and say so if none does.
- If the filter needs a server-side marker that does not exist, file that on objectstack as the companion.
